scope: Engine fix (image destination delimiter now uses findImageAltEnd-derived alt boundary via directImageDestinationSource, mirroring link's position-aware directLinkDestinationSource), 324-fixture digest chain, 21-variant x 12-candidate destructive replay, four in-place destructive-oracle reversions, link-shape-36 control group, digest recomputation, and the two NUL-character-reference deferral P2s.

verdicts.notes: evaluateProblem real-engine replay across all 12 candidates (not one representative), 21 variants x 12 = 252 cases, mismatch 0: plain image/ordinary title/"a ] b"/"a ( b"/"a ]( b" overcapture-noise/poison-title "title ]()"/nested-bracket alt/escaped-bracket alt/escaped-]()-alt (two forms)/direct U+FFFD/single-char 'a'/nested-alt+poison-title all matched; empty alt/empty()/empty(   )/empty(<>)/NUL destination/ZWSP destination/NUL alt/ZWSP alt all fail. All 96 fail cases across the matrix produce exactly one repairInstruction sentence (the committed visible-text sentence). Four destructive-oracle probes applied directly to structural.ts and reverted after each (sha256 diffed before/after): (1) restoring the legacy raw.lastIndexOf("](") delimiter search reproduces RED on poison-title and nested-alt+poison-title, 12/12 each; (2) a naive over-fix rejecting any title outright reproduces RED on all 6 title-bearing matched lines, 72/72, confirming the matched-line set catches over-blocking; (3) a naive first-match indexOf oracle (in place of the alt-end-aware scan) reproduces RED only on the two escaped-]()-alt fixtures, 24/24 -- discriminating exactly where a ](-only probe cannot, matching the fixture file's committed rationale comment; (4) removing the raw term from hasMeaningfulDestination leaks NUL destination to matched (12/12 RED) while ZWSP destination stays correctly failing, confirming the raw term is the NUL-specific defense (mdast normalizes destination NUL to U+FFFD, which the parsed-side check alone would accept). Verified directLinkDestinationSource (link path) is untouched by this diff and remains position-aware; confirmed via git diff against e9a0f9ef that only nodeHasMeaningfulInlineDestination/rawImageAlt/findImageAltEnd/directImageDestinationSource changed. Cross-checked the link-shape 36-problem poison-title control group: all 36 remain matched (unaffected), while the 12 image problems flip from fail to matched. Independently recomputed manifestDigest and engineContractDigest via buildImageBatch029Artifacts and confirmed exact match against the values bound in review scope. bank:batch:image-029:check gate 7/7 PASS; fixture file totals 324 = 12x27 uniform. Separately reproduced both NUL-character-reference Codex P2s (id 3881196381, 3881416326): literal NUL, �, �, and directly-typed U+FFFD all normalize to the identical U+FFFD after mdast parsing (confirmed via direct AST inspection), so alt/destination axis shows literal NUL fail 12/12 while �/� forms all matched 12/12 (uncaught) on both axes -- confirms the P2s reproduce as described. Confirmed via git show that imageBatch027/028Problems.ts do not exist on origin/main, i.e. the image problem surface itself is new to this PR chain, so this is pre-existing rawNullCount/hasMeaningfulParsedCharacters semantics surfacing on a new consumer, not a regression introduced between e9a0f9ef and 2f06a731 -- deferral to a follow-up issue (bundled with the committed direct-U+FFFD-matched decision) is the correct classification. Also independently tested the proposed 'block U+FFFD outright' alternative: adding U+FFFD to hasMeaningfulCharacters' exclusion class does uniformly fail all four NUL-origin forms (12/12 each) but also flips the already-committed 'direct-typed U+FFFD is matched' boundary to fail (12/12), which would make the current visible-text feedback sentence false since U+FFFD is visible -- confirms this alternative is a trap as characterized, not a cheap fix. All four destructive probes and this fifth exploratory one were reverted immediately after measurement with sha256 diffed before/after against 55d579078bd382451328561ba370c362ec2f39293a2d68037611011595eca208.
